api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Aggregates.Ag.title: Enum AggregateFaultOrigin | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Aggregates.Ag.summary: Enum AggregateFaultOrigin Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Aggregates Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Identifies the lifecycle operation that made an aggregate instance unsafe for further domain use. The origin distinguishes deterministic replay failures from live command or event-tracking failures in diagnostics. public enum AggregateFaultOrigin Fields CommandHandling = 3 Indicates that a command handler raised an unexpected exception and may have left in-memory state uncertain. EventApplication = 0 Indicates that an event handler failed while applying a newly emitted event to live aggregate state. EventTracking = 1 Indicates that metadata creation or uncommitted-event tracking failed after an event was applied. Rehydration = 2 Indicates that a persisted stream could not be deserialized, validated structurally, or replayed.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Catalog.Event.summary: Class EventContractCatalogVerifier Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Catalog Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Compares a catalogue against a published baseline and reports incompatible changes. public static class EventContractCatalogVerifier Inheritance object EventContractCatalogVerifier Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Enforces the event-evolution rules mechanically: additive optional properties and new contracts pass, renames, removals and type changes fail. The escape hatch for anything on the forbidden list is a new contract, never an edit to an existing one, because historic events keep their stored payload forever and must still deserialize into the current CLR type. The rules are deliberately not scoped by event version. Replay restores the persisted event-version metadata after payload construction, so bumping a version neither breaks nor legitimizes anything — a changed version is reported as a signal, not as permission. Methods Verify(EventContractCatalogDocument, EventContractCatalogDocument) Verifies a catalogue against its baseline. public static IReadOnlyList<EventContractViolation> Verify(EventContractCatalogDocument baseline, EventContractCatalogDocument current) Parameters baseline EventContractCatalogDocument The published catalogue the application must stay compatible with. current EventContractCatalogDocument The catalogue produced by the current build. api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Catalog.Event.summary: Class EventContractDescriptor Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Catalog Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Describes one declared event contract as it appears on the wire. public sealed record EventContractDescriptor : IEquatable<EventContractDescriptor> Inheritance object EventContractDescriptor Implements IEquatable<EventContractDescriptor> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks On a broker shared by several applications, the Contract name is a cross-application namespace that nothing reserves. Two applications can pick the same name for different payloads, and the mismatch surfaces only when a foreign consumer fails to interpret an event. A catalogue makes that mechanically detectable before deployment instead. Everything here is resolved at compile time by the bundled generator, so the descriptor reflects the declaration rather than any particular event instance. Constructors EventContractDescriptor() public EventContractDescriptor() Properties AggregateName Gets the stable aggregate contract name the event belongs to. public required string AggregateName { get; init; } Property Value string ClrType Gets the declaring CLR type, for diagnostics only. It is not part of the contract. public required string ClrType { get; init; } Property Value string Contract Gets the stable contract name declared by EventContractAttribute. public required string Contract { get; init; } Property Value string EventVersion Gets the positive current write version declared by EventContractAttribute, or null when reading a legacy catalogue that did not resolve one. public int? EventVersion { get; init; } Property Value int? Remarks The generator reads the attribute's integer literal or named compile-time constant directly. A non-positive declaration is reported and omitted rather than producing a new descriptor with a null version. Null remains supported here so older committed catalogue documents can still be compared. Fields Gets the serialized payload fields, ordered by name. public required IReadOnlyList<EventContractField> Fields { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<EventContractField> FieldsFingerprint Gets a stable hash over Fields, for compact artifact diffs and integrity checks. public required string FieldsFingerprint { get; init; } Property Value string Remarks The hash alone cannot classify a change: adding an optional property is allowed without a new version, renaming one is not, and both change the hash. Verification therefore always compares Fields and never trusts this derived value as compatibility evidence by itself. Lifecycle Gets whether the event establishes, changes, or terminates the aggregate stream. public AggregateLifecycle Lifecycle { get; init; } Property Value AggregateLifecycle Uniqueness Gets write-side uniqueness declarations, or null when this descriptor predates their capture. Null is incomplete metadata, not an assertion that the event declares no reservations. public EventContractUniqueness? Properties AggregateId Gets the locked aggregate identity. IIdentity AggregateId { get; } Property Value IIdentity AggregateName Gets the locked aggregate contract name retained for diagnostics. IAggregateName AggregateName { get; } Property Value IAggregateName CreationDate Gets when lock ownership began. DateTime CreationDate { get; } Property Value DateTime IsReleased Gets a value indicating whether ownership has already been released explicitly, by disposing this lock. bool IsReleased { get; } Property Value bool Remarks It reports the holder's own release only. A lock whose backing session or stream was lost underneath it still reports false here; IsHeldAsync(CancellationToken) is the member that can see that. RequestId Gets the request that owns the lock. IRequestId RequestId { get; } Property Value IRequestId Methods IsHeldAsync(CancellationToken) Checks whether this lock is still held, including whether whatever holds it remotely is still alive. ValueTask<bool> IsHeldAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token for the check. Returns ValueTask<bool> true when ownership is still in force; false after an explicit release or when the implementation detected that the lock was lost, for example because the PostgreSQL session holding it ended or the Gateway ended the lock's stream. Remarks Added in Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd 19.2.0. The default implementation can only see an explicit release and returns IsReleased == false; an implementation backed by a session or a stream overrides it to probe that session or stream. A result of false is final: a lost lock is not regained. The probe detects and reports, it does not protect a write. CommandExecutor calls it once before committing and still commits when it returns false, because the commit's transaction lock and concurrency-token comparison already decide an overlapping write. Exceptions OperationCanceledException cancellationToken was cancelled.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Repositories..title: Interface IAggregateLockPort | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Repositories..summary: Interface IAggregateLockPort Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Repositories Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Coordinates exclusive aggregate ownership and returns a disposable lease to the successful caller. public interface IAggregateLockPort Remarks This is the application-facing DDD port. It is strongly typed over the aggregate identity, applies a bounded retry policy, and is what CommandExecutor depends on. An application implements or registers it; it does not talk to a database itself. Do not confuse it with Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Locks.IAggregateLockStore, which is the PostgreSQL advisory-lock store on the persistence side: untyped, no retry policy, and one layer below this port. An adapter implements this interface over that store. The Port suffix names that layer difference, which the former name ILockRepository left to the documentation. api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Results.Aggre.title: Class AggregateCommitReceipt | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Results.Aggre.summary: Class AggregateCommitReceipt Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Results Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Names exactly what one successful aggregate commit wrote, so a caller can refer to that commit afterwards instead of guessing where the write side got to. public sealed record AggregateCommitReceipt : IEquatable<AggregateCommitReceipt> Inheritance object AggregateCommitReceipt Implements IEquatable<AggregateCommitReceipt> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks A commit is durable the moment it succeeds, but the read side reaches it later. Every question a caller can ask about that gap — "is my change visible yet", "which token do I send with the next command" — needs a name for the commit, and before this receipt existed the write path returned success and nothing else. The token was reachable only by reading a projection, which is itself subject to the very delay the caller was trying to reason about. EventSequence is the watermark. It is the last event of this commit and the one position the MongoDB projection pipeline orders by, so "the read model has caught up with my commit" is exactly applied >= EventSequence. Compare with >= and never with ==: delivery is at-least-once and later events may already be applied. AggregateRevision is not a substitute. One commit may emit several events, so a revision maps to a range of sequences rather than a position, and the projection does not order by it. AggregateConcurrencyToken is not a substitute either: it is opaque and random, so it supports equality and optimistic concurrency but carries no ordering at all. Constructors AggregateCommitReceipt() public AggregateCommitReceipt() Properties AggregateConcurrencyToken Gets the token the aggregate now carries. Send it back with the next modifying command instead of reading it from a projection that may not have caught up yet. public required AggregateConcurrencyToken AggregateConcurrencyToken { get; init; } Property Value AggregateConcurrencyToken AggregateId Gets the globally unique aggregate identifier the commit was written for. public required string AggregateId { get; init; } Property Value string AggregateName Gets the stable aggregate contract name the commit was written for. public required string AggregateName { get; init; } Property Value string AggregateRevision Gets the client-visible revision this commit advanced the aggregate to. public required long AggregateRevision { get; init; } Property Value long AlreadyCommitted Gets whether this receipt describes a commit that already existed rather than one this call performed. public bool AlreadyCommitted { get; init; } Property Value bool Remarks A retry of an ambiguous outcome repeats the request identity, finds the original commit, and writes nothing. The receipt still describes a durable commit and is just as valid to wait on — but a caller counting writes, charging for work, or emitting an integration event on success needs to know that this call was not the one that did it. EventCount Gets how many domain events this commit wrote, each of which becomes one bus message. public required int EventCount { get; init; } Property Value int EventIds Gets the identifiers of the events this commit wrote, in commit order. public IReadOnlyList<string> EventIds { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> Remarks Diagnostic detail rather than a barrier: publication and projection progress are both asked by stream position, which stays one indexed range lookup however many events a commit contains. These identifiers are what correlates a commit with individual outbox rows, bus messages and dead letters. EventSequence Gets the one-based stream position of the last event in this commit, which is the watermark a read model must reach for this commit to be visible. public required long EventSequence { get; init; } Property Value long FirstEventSequence Gets the one-based stream position of the first event in this commit. public required long FirstEventSequence { get; init; } Property Value long IsDeleted Gets whether this commit terminated the stream. A deleted aggregate loses its merged projection rather than gaining a newer one, so a reader waiting for this commit must expect a removal, not an update. public required bool IsDeleted { get; init; } Property Value bool PreviousAggregateConcurrencyToken Gets the token the commit expected the aggregate to be at, or null when this commit created the stream. public AggregateConcurrencyToken? PreviousAggregateConcurrencyToken { get; init; } Property Value AggregateConcurrencyToken RequestId Gets the request identity the commit was written under. Retrying the same request identity is idempotent, and the event store records it, so it is also how a receipt can be recovered after an ambiguous transport outcome. public required string RequestId { get; init; } Property Value string TenantId Gets the tenant context carried by the committed events, when the application uses one. public string? TenantId { get; init; } Property Value string Methods Equals(AggregateCommitReceipt?) public bool Equals(AggregateCommitReceipt? other) Parameters other AggregateCommitReceipt Returns bool Equals(object?) public override bool Equals(object? obj) Parameters obj object Returns bool FromCommittedEvents(IReadOnlyCollection<IStoredEvent>, bool) Rebuilds the receipt of a commit that is already durable, from the events it wrote. public static AggregateCommitReceipt FromCommittedEvents(IReadOnlyCollection<IStoredEvent> events, bool alreadyCommitted) Parameters events IReadOnlyCollection<IStoredEvent> Every event of exactly one commit — one aggregate, one request identity — in any order. alreadyCommitted bool Whether this describes an earlier commit rather than a fresh one. Returns AggregateCommitReceipt The receipt describing that commit. Remarks Used where the commit was performed by someone else and has to be reported faithfully: a repeated request identity whose original commit is being described, and the persistence gateway reporting a duplicate it detected. In those cases the values a fresh commit would have computed describe a commit that never happened, so they must be read back rather than assumed. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when events is null. ArgumentException Thrown when the collection is empty or its events do not all belong to one commit of one aggregate. api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Results.Domai.title: Enum DomainErrorCategory | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Results.Domai.summary: Enum DomainErrorCategory Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Results Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Classifies a domain or application failure independently of its stable error code. public enum DomainErrorCategory Fields Authorization = 7 Indicates that the caller is known but is not permitted to perform this operation. Distinct from Validation: the command is well-formed and the aggregate state permits the operation in principle, but this caller may not perform it. An API layer maps the two differently — typically 400 against 403 — so reporting an authorization failure as a validation failure is a wire defect rather than a naming preference. Per-command authorization belongs in ValidateAggregateAsync, because that is the first stage at which the aggregate's own state is available: ValidateInputAsync runs before the lock and before rehydration, so it cannot decide "may this caller act on this aggregate". This category does not authenticate anyone and does not decide policy. It classifies a decision the application has already made. Concurrency = 4 Indicates an optimistic or pessimistic concurrency conflict. Conflict = 3 Indicates a business conflict such as a unique-value violation. Infrastructure = 5 Indicates a persistence, transport, or other infrastructure failure. NotFound = 2 Indicates that a requested domain object does not exist. Serialization = 6 Indicates an event or value serialization failure. Unknown = 0 Indicates that no more specific category is known. Validation = 1 Indicates invalid command input or a violated domain invariant.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Snapshots.Agg.title: Class AggregateSnapshotUnreadableException | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Snapshots.Agg.summary: Class AggregateSnapshotUnreadableException Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Snapshots Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Signals that a persisted snapshot exists but this build cannot interpret its payload, so the aggregate has to be rebuilt from its events instead. public sealed class AggregateSnapshotUnreadableException : InvalidOperationException, ISerializable Inheritance object Exception SystemException InvalidOperationException AggregateSnapshotUnreadableException Implements ISerializable Inherited Members Exception.GetBaseException() Exception.ToString() Exception.GetType() Exception.TargetSite Exception.Message Exception.Data Exception.InnerException Exception.HelpLink Exception.Source Exception.HResult Exception.StackTrace object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A snapshot is a replaceable cache and never the source of truth, so an unreadable one must not make a stream unwritable. This exception exists to separate that recoverable case from the failures that are not recoverable: a snapshot addressing a different aggregate, invalid metadata, or an event in the tail that cannot be replayed all keep throwing their original exception, because rebuilding would not help and the silence would hide an infrastructure defect. CommandExecutor handles this automatically — it discards the aggregate, reloads the complete event stream and logs a warning. Code that rehydrates by hand should do the same: catch this exception, build a fresh aggregate, and call Load(IReadOnlyCollection<IStoredEvent>) with the full stream. The instance that threw is faulted and must be discarded. In practice this means a state type whose shape changed since the snapshot was written — adding or removing a single property is enough, because the payload has to round-trip losslessly — or whose constructor or a value converter now rejects what an old snapshot contains. Any exception raised while deserializing the payload is reported this way except cancellation, whatever its type. The other cause is a row written by a platform version that used a different snapshot format, which is what makes changing that format a self-healing operation rather than a migration. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when innerException is null. Properties AggregateId Gets the identity of the aggregate the snapshot belongs to. public string AggregateId { get; } Property Value string AggregateName Gets the stable aggregate contract name the snapshot belongs to. public string AggregateName { get; } Property Value string AggregateVersion Gets the event position the unreadable snapshot represents. public long AggregateVersion { get; } Property Value long SnapshotFormatVersion Gets the serialized state contract version recorded on the unreadable snapshot. public int SnapshotFormatVersion { get; } Property Value int

api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.UniqueValues..summary: Enum UniqueCompare Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.UniqueValues Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Controls when an annotated event property contributes a concrete value or placeholder reservation to a uniqueness index. public enum UniqueCompare Fields Always = 0 Always includes the property and substitutes an empty value for null; without serialization that empty value is blank and therefore releases instead of reserving. IfNotNull = 1 Includes the property only when its value is not null; a blank text value still releases instead of reserving. IfNotNullOrWhitespace = 2 Includes the property only when its text representation is not null, empty, or whitespace. Remarks An excluded value produces a dummy reservation that releases the aggregate's previous value for the key. Independently of the strategy, legacy scalar extraction treats a resulting string that is empty or whitespace as no value and releases as well, because every store trims before comparing and no store can hold a blank reservation. Serialized and JSON-array values are JSON text and therefore never blank.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Dependen.title: Class EventBusServiceCollectionExtensions | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Dependen.summary: Class EventBusServiceCollectionExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.DependencyInjection Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.dll Registers the logical-to-physical event-bus resolver and its transport provider factories. public static class EventBusServiceCollectionExtensions Inheritance object EventBusServiceCollectionExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods AddDevboneEventBus(IServiceCollection, EventBusTargetsOptions) Registers the event bus from validated target options. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneEventBus(this IServiceCollection services, EventBusTargetsOptions targets) Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. targets EventBusTargetsOptions Logical-to-physical bus targets. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks The resolver is a singleton and owns the broker connections it creates. It is registered so the container disposes it: ConfiguredEventBusResolver is IAsyncDisposable, and a resolver that is never disposed leaks producer and consumer connections for the process lifetime. Registration opens no connection. Provider factories create configured adapters; network resources are opened only by an explicit publish, subscribe, start or readiness call. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when an argument is null. AddDevboneEventBus(IServiceCollection, EventBusTargetsOptions, IEnumerable<IEventBusProviderFactory>) Registers the event bus with explicit transport provider factories. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneEventBus(this IServiceCollection services, EventBusTargetsOptions targets, IEnumerable<IEventBusProviderFactory> providerFactories) Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. targets EventBusTargetsOptions Logical-to-physical bus targets. providerFactories IEnumerable<IEventBusProviderFactory> Provider factories keyed by transport name. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks Use this overload to pass the transport factories explicitly instead of resolving the ones the transport packages registered, for example to restrict an application to one transport. It cannot add a transport the platform does not ship: targets accept Kafka and RabbitMQ only. The other overload registers no transport itself; it uses whatever AddDevboneKafkaEventBus or AddDevboneRabbitMqEventBus registered. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when an argument is null.

Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks Call this alongside AddDevboneEventBus, in either order: the resolver reads the registered provider factories when it is first constructed, not when it is registered. Referencing this package is what brings Confluent.Kafka into the application. An application that uses one broker should reference only that broker's transport package, which is the reason the transports do not live in Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.D.summary: Class OutboxDispatcherServiceCollectionExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.DependencyInjection Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.dll Registers the durable outbox dispatcher that claims persisted outbox rows and publishes them. public static class OutboxDispatcherServiceCollectionExtensions Inheritance object OutboxDispatcherServiceCollectionExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods AddDevboneEventResend(IServiceCollection, ResendOptions) Registers the operator-requested outbox replay executor. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneEventResend(this IServiceCollection services, ResendOptions options) Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. options ResendOptions Replay execution settings. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks Requires AddDevboneEventStore and AddDevboneEventBus. Every instance may host this: the request row's claim decides which one executes a given request, so no leader election or singleton deployment is needed. A replay reaches every consumer of the affected streams, including applications that do not belong to the requester. On a shared broker, confirm that foreign consumers are idempotent before enabling it. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when an argument is null. AddDevboneOutboxDispatcher(IServiceCollection, OutboxDispatcherOptions) Registers the outbox dispatcher and, in embedded mode, the hosted service that runs it. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneOutboxDispatcher(this IServiceCollection services, OutboxDispatcherOptions options) Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. options OutboxDispatcherOptions Dispatcher settings including the owning event-store id and worker id. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks Requires AddDevboneEventStore (for IOutboxStore and IOutboxNotificationListener) and AddDevboneEventBus (for IEventBusResolver). Publication is deliberately separate from persistence: a commit is durable once the event and its outbox row are written, and delivery is a later, independently retried step. Delivery is at-least-once. The dispatcher claims a row with a lease, publishes, then settles; a crash between publish and settle re-delivers after the lease expires, which is why consumers must settle manually and deduplicate. When the composition registers an EventStoreIdentity, as AddDevboneEventSourcing does, the dispatcher must name the same store: resolving it otherwise throws InvalidOperationException, so the host does not start. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when an argument is null.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.R.summary: Class ResendProcessor Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.Resend Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.dll Executes one claimed resend request by republishing already published outbox envelopes. public sealed class ResendProcessor Inheritance object ResendProcessor Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The envelope bytes are republished verbatim, exactly as they were first delivered. That is the property the whole feature rests on: a projection compares an incoming event with the one it already stored, and a byte-identical event is a no-op. Rebuilding the envelope instead — a fresh timestamp, a new trace context — would make every replayed event look like an identifier reused with different content, which dead-letters rather than repairs. Progress is reported against the claim. If the lease was taken over, the run stops immediately instead of racing the instance that now owns the request. DeadLetterHeaderNames Header names a transport adapter adds when it moves a message it cannot read to the configured poison-message dead-letter stream. The message keeps its original body and headers; these describe why and from where. The original may hold personal data: keep dead-letter streams under explicit retention and access control, and never copy their content into logs or telemetry. EventBusNames The one transport-neutral naming rule for what a subscription and its queue are built from. Both brokers read some characters as more than a name: a Kafka topic starting with ^ is a regular-expression subscription, * and # are wildcards in a RabbitMQ binding key, and a RabbitMQ queue is named {consumer}.{stream} or {consumer}.{instance}.{stream}, which is ambiguous as soon as a consumer name or an instance identity holds a dot. Each of those silently delivers another stream's messages; the rule refuses them, RabbitMQ's reserved amq. prefix, and names that would exceed the 255-byte queue-name limit. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence..summary: Class EventPersistenceGatewayServiceCollectionExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence.Gateway.DependencyInjection Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence.Gateway.dll Registers the Event Persistence Gateway in a host's service collection. public static class EventPersistenceGatewayServiceCollectionExtensions Inheritance object EventPersistenceGatewayServiceCollectionExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods AddDevboneEventPersistenceGateway(IServiceCollection, IConfiguration) Binds and validates the Gateway's configuration and registers its services: routing, the event store per target, the bus resolver, the stored-event mappers, field protection when a target enables it, the lock-stream bound, the embedded outbox dispatchers and one outbox inventory sampler per target. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneEventPersistenceGateway(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration) Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. configuration IConfiguration The configuration holding the Gateway's sections. Returns IServiceCollection The service collection. Remarks The configuration is read from the sections EventPersistenceGateway, EventStoreTargets, EventBusTargets and AggregateRouting (required), ProjectionCompatibility and EventMessageSizeLimits (optional), and KeyService (required only when a target enables field protection). Pass a section of the host's configuration to nest them below a prefix of the host's choosing. Everything is validated here, so a misconfigured host fails while it is built rather than on its first request. No broker transport is registered: the host registers the transport of every bus target it configures, for example AddDevboneKafkaEventBus. Readiness, telemetry export and the shutdown timeout are the host's decisions as well. Exceptions InvalidOperationException A required section is missing. ArgumentException A section holds a value the Gateway refuses.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence..summary: Class EventPersistenceEndpoints Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence.Gateway.Endpoints Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence.Gateway.dll Maps the versioned Event Persistence Gateway HTTP API. public static class EventPersistenceEndpoints Inheritance object EventPersistenceEndpoints Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods MapDevboneEventPersistenceGateway(WebApplication) Maps the Gateway's /v1 endpoints and adds the two middlewares they run behind: one that maps the Gateway's failures to its error contract, and one that authenticates the caller's API key. public static WebApplication MapDevboneEventPersistenceGateway(this WebApplication app) Parameters app WebApplication The web application. Returns WebApplication The web application. Remarks Both middlewares act on the Gateway's own endpoints only, so a host that serves endpoints of its own beside them keeps its authentication and error handling for those, and its probes stay anonymous. Conversely the host's authorization does not apply to the Gateway's endpoints: they are marked anonymous for it, because the Gateway authenticates its callers by API key. A request that matches no endpoint passes through and is answered by the host. The key is checked before the request body is read. Register the services first with AddDevboneEventPersistenceGateway.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.C.summary: Class ReadModelWaiterOptions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client.Configuration Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client.dll Configures bounded read-your-writes waiting against the projection database. public sealed class ReadModelWaiterOptions Inheritance object ReadModelWaiterOptions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Constructors ReadModelWaiterOptions() public ReadModelWaiterOptions() Fields SECTION_NAME The configuration section these options bind from. public const string SECTION_NAME = "ReadModelWaiter" Field Value string Properties ConnectionString Gets or sets the MongoDB connection string of the projection database. Required unless the application supplies its own database instance. public string ConnectionString { get; set; } Property Value string DatabaseName Gets or sets the projection database name. It must be the database the projection pipeline writes; a waiter pointed at an empty database reports a projection that never catches up. public string DatabaseName { get; set; } Property Value string DefaultTimeout Gets or sets the budget used when a request names none. Deliberately short: past a second or two a caller is better served by a deferred response than by a held connection. public TimeSpan DefaultTimeout { get; set; } Property Value TimeSpan MaximumConcurrentWaits Gets or sets how many waits may be in flight at once. Reaching it sheds further waits immediately instead of queueing them, so a projection outage degrades responses rather than exhausting the host. public int MaximumConcurrentWaits { get; set; } Property Value int MaximumTimeout Gets or sets the largest budget a single request may ask for. Requests above it are clamped, so one caller cannot hold a slot for as long as it likes. public TimeSpan MaximumTimeout { get; set; } Property Value TimeSpan PendingRetryAfter Gets or sets the delay a non-blocking barrier check reports when a barrier is still pending. public TimeSpan PendingRetryAfter { get; set; } Property Value TimeSpan Remarks One value for every pending reason, on purpose. A cause-aware delay — longer for a stream that is replaying than for a projection one event behind — is plausible and unmeasured, and a guessed heuristic here would be indistinguishable from a tuned one until it was wrong in production. PollInterval Gets or sets how often a pending wait re-reads the projection. The floor on how long a wait outlives the write it is waiting for, and the ceiling on how much load waiting adds. public TimeSpan PollInterval { get; set; } Property Value TimeSpan RegistryCacheDuration Gets or sets how long the published projection registry is cached. public TimeSpan RegistryCacheDuration { get; set; } Property Value TimeSpan Remarks Definitions change at deployment boundaries and availability changes when worker capabilities start or expire, while the registry is read on the acceptance path of every request that names a projection. Short-lived rather than permanent, so deployments and expired leases become visible without restarting the API host. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.C.summary: Interface IReadModelConsistencyBarrier Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client.Consistency Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client.dll Answers, once and without blocking, whether the read models have observed a set of committed positions. public interface IReadModelConsistencyBarrier Remarks This is the primitive. IReadModelWaiter is a bounded wait built on top of it, for the case where a caller wants to hold its request briefly; everything that returns early and lets the client come back — a queued response, a status endpoint, a polling orchestrator — uses this instead and owns its own retry rhythm. One call, one batch. Barriers are grouped by layer and aggregate type into one keyed query each, so checking fifty positions does not become fifty round trips. Read-only: it never claims, mutates or advances anything. It is not free, though: an unreached group costs up to four sequential queries per call (progress, registry when its cache expired, dead-letter evidence and the stall probe), and concurrent callers are not coalesced. Pace repeated checks by RetryAfter. Methods CheckAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<ReadModelBarrier>, CancellationToken) Checks a batch of barriers once. An empty batch is satisfied. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<ReadModelBarrierResult> The combined state and one progress entry per barrier. Remarks An unreadable progress store is reported as a failed barrier rather than thrown: it is one more state a caller has to handle, not a reason to lose the commit it is asking about. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.C.title: Interface IReadModelWaiter | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.C.summary: Interface IReadModelWaiter Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client.Consistency Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client.dll Waits, within a bounded budget, until a framework-standard projection reflects one committed aggregate change. public interface IReadModelWaiter Remarks A convenience over IReadModelConsistencyBarrier, for the case where a caller wants to hold its request briefly and answer with the result. Anything that returns early and lets the client come back — a queued response, a status endpoint, an orchestrator owning its own retry rhythm — should use the barrier check directly instead of blocking here. This buys read-your-writes for one caller, not consistency for the system. Nobody else's read becomes more consistent, no ordering guarantee changes, and nothing here makes the platform's delivery anything other than at-least-once. It closes exactly one gap: the caller that just wrote something and immediately reads it back. Use it per request, never as a global mode. Waiting on every write puts a database round trip and the projection's own failure modes on the critical path of the write, which is the opposite of why the read side is separate. Wait after the command completed, never inside it. The command holds an aggregate lock for its duration, so waiting before it returns adds the projection latency to the lock hold time and to every other writer of that aggregate. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.C.summary: Class ReadModelWaiter Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client.Consistency Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client.dll Waits for projection progress by polling, with every wait on the same aggregate type served by one shared query per tick. public sealed class ReadModelWaiter : IReadModelWaiter, IDisposable Inheritance object ReadModelWaiter Implements IReadModelWaiter IDisposable Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Polling rather than a broker subscription, on purpose. The pipeline's completion signals are internal addresses with per-aggregate ordering topology: an API host subscribing to them needs its own consumer group or queue per instance, competes with the single active consumer the pipeline relies on, loses every pending wait when it restarts, and still races against notifications that passed before the request arrived. On top of that the merged signal is published only when derived handlers are registered, so in a zero-code deployment there is nothing to subscribe to at all. What makes polling affordable is that the cost is bounded by the number of waiting requests rather than by throughput, and that one tick serves every wait on the same projection and aggregate type in a single keyed query. A thousand requests waiting on one aggregate produce one query per tick, not a thousand. Registered as a singleton. The shared poll loop is what the coalescing is built on, and a scoped instance would give every request its own. An API host therefore only places an immutable request. A worker with RefoldRequests.Enabled accepts requests from its configured requester and refuses those of any other, then runs the refold as if requested through the pipeline's own refold service. Every request carries the requester configured in ProjectionRefoldRequesterOptions. That value tells requests apart and is recorded as the audit actor; it is not a credential, so anything that can write to the projection database can place a request. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.D.summary: Class ProjectionServiceCollectionExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.DependencyInjection Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Registers the projection pipeline: the always-on raw and merged layers, the adapters of the selected transport, and the derived layer that carries application-owned query models. public static class ProjectionServiceCollectionExtensions Inheritance object ProjectionServiceCollectionExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods AddDevboneEventProjection(IServiceCollection, IConfiguration, string) Registers the complete projection pipeline with options bound from configuration. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneEventProjection(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration, string sectionName = "EventProjection") Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. configuration IConfiguration Configuration containing the projection section. sectionName string The configuration section name. Defaults to SECTION_NAME. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks This package carries no broker client. Register the transport for your broker in the same composition root — AddDevboneKafkaEventProjection() from Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Kafka or AddDevboneRabbitMqEventProjection() from Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.RabbitMq — in either order, and select it with Transport. Register application query models with AddProjectionHandler<THandler>(IServiceCollection) after calling this method. Almost every registration here is a singleton, because the pipeline holds broker connections and a MongoDB client for the lifetime of the host. Two kinds are scoped: handlers, which each invocation resolves from a new scope, and ProjectionRepairService and ProjectionRefoldService together with their authorization policies, which an application resolves in the scope of the request it serves. This is the only supported way to compose the processors; replace a store by registering your own implementation of its port after this call, because the last registration of a service wins. Static configuration is validated through ValidateOnStart. Store initialization then connects to MongoDB and rejects a standalone server before consumer workers start, because raw persistence requires transactions on an initialized replica set or sharded cluster. AddProjectionHandler<THandler>(IServiceCollection) Registers one application-owned derived projection handler. public static IServiceCollection AddProjectionHandler<THandler>(this IServiceCollection services) where THandler : class, IProjectionHandler Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Type Parameters THandler The handler implementation. Remarks Handlers observe merged state at least as new as the event they are handling, and inherit ordering, dedupe, and retry from the pipeline. Because delivery is at-least-once and the merged document may already reflect later events, handlers must be idempotent. Handler exceptions retry through the selected transport and terminally dead-letter at MaximumDerivedHandlerAttemptCount without advancing that handler's checkpoint. The handler is registered scoped and resolved from a new scope for every invocation, so it may depend on scoped services such as an Entity Framework DbContext; the scope is disposed when the invocation ends. One additional instance is resolved at startup to read ProjectionName, DefinitionVersion and CanHandle(string), which must therefore not depend on per-invocation state. Before 14.0.0 handlers were singletons.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.M.summary: Class ProjectionCompatibilityOptions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.MongoDb.Configuration Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.MongoDb.dll Configures fail-fast limits shared by event producers and MongoDB projection consumers. public sealed class ProjectionCompatibilityOptions Inheritance object ProjectionCompatibilityOptions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Constructors ProjectionCompatibilityOptions() public ProjectionCompatibilityOptions() Fields DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_AGGREGATE_STATE_BYTES Default maximum BSON size of the final aggregate state validated at commit. public const int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_AGGREGATE_STATE_BYTES = 1048576 Field Value int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_DOCUMENT_DEPTH Default maximum supported JSON and BSON nesting depth. public const int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_DOCUMENT_DEPTH = 64 Field Value int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES Default maximum UTF-8 or BSON size of one event payload. public const int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 262144 Field Value int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_INTERMEDIATE_STATE_BYTES Default conservative upper bound for intermediate states in a multi-event commit. public const int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_INTERMEDIATE_STATE_BYTES = 12582912 Field Value int Properties IsEnabled Gets or sets whether the write-side commit guard runs. Enabled by default. public bool IsEnabled { get; init; } Property Value bool Remarks Turning this off is the supported escape hatch for an application that provably does not project to MongoDB. It disables ValidateCommit(string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>) only, so aggregate commits stop being checked against BSON representability and MongoDB size limits. It deliberately does not disable the read-side checks in the projection pipeline: those guard an actual MongoDB write, where the limits are physical rather than a policy. Disabling it in a system that does project to MongoDB moves the failure from a recoverable command error to a permanently dead-lettered projection message and a read model that silently diverges. There is no supported repair for that, because the offending event is already immutable. MaximumAggregateStateBytes Gets or sets the maximum BSON size of the final aggregate state. public int MaximumAggregateStateBytes { get; init; } Property Value int MaximumDocumentDepth Gets or sets the maximum supported object and array nesting depth. public int MaximumDocumentDepth { get; init; } Property Value int MaximumEventPayloadBytes Gets or sets the maximum UTF-8 and BSON size of one event payload. public int MaximumEventPayloadBytes { get; init; } Property Value int MaximumIntermediateStateBytes Gets or sets the conservative maximum for the previous projection plus every patch in one commit. This protects event-by-event read processing without reproducing the projection on the write side. public int MaximumIntermediateStateBytes { get; init; } Property Value int Methods Validate() Validates configured limits before they are used for a commit. public void Validate() Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when a limit is non-positive or internally inconsistent.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.O.summary: Class ProjectionTraceContext Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Observability Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Carries the W3C trace context across the projection pipeline's own publications, so one domain event's raw, merged and derived stages appear in the trace of the command that produced it. public static class ProjectionTraceContext Inheritance object ProjectionTraceContext Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks This is the transport-neutral half of the propagation. A transport writes CurrentHeaders() as message headers on every internal publication and maps the same two headers of a consumed message into TraceParent and TraceState; the stages continue that context with StartActivity(string, ActivityKind, string?, string?). The header names are the canonical TRACE_PARENT and TRACE_STATE the event bus uses for domain events. A stage's activity is a child of the remote context, as the event bus consumers' are: at-least-once redelivery produces a second child of the same parent, which is what a redelivery is. The context lives in transport headers only and never in a message body, so it cannot change a message key, its ordering, the byte equality that deduplicates a stored event, or settlement. A message without the headers — one published by an older worker during a rolling deployment, or without an active trace — is processed exactly as before under a new root. Methods CurrentHeaders() Gets the W3C headers that carry the current activity's trace context on an internal publication. public static IReadOnlyList<KeyValuePair<string, string>> CurrentHeaders() Returns IReadOnlyList<KeyValuePair<string, string>> TRACE_PARENT and, when the activity has one, TRACE_STATE; empty when no activity is current or the current one does not use the W3C identifier format. StartActivity(string, ActivityKind, string?, string?) Starts one projection-pipeline activity as a child of a remote W3C context. public static Activity? StartActivity(string operationName, ActivityKind kind, string? traceParent, string? traceState) Parameters operationName string Low-cardinality operation name of the stage. kind ActivityKind Activity kind. traceParent string Remote traceparent value, or null when the message carried none. traceState string Remote tracestate value belonging to traceParent, or null. Returns Activity The started activity, parented on the remote context when traceParent parses, otherwise on the ambient activity or as a new root; null when no listener samples the pipeline's source. Remarks A missing or malformed traceparent never fails processing: tracing is diagnostic, and a value from a foreign producer must not decide whether a message is projected.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.summary: Interface IProjectionCheckpointStore Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Persistence Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Records how far each application query model has processed each aggregate. public interface IProjectionCheckpointStore Remarks The raw and merged layers need no checkpoint: their own document already records the position it was carried to, and a second copy would add a write to the pipeline's hot path plus a value that can disagree with the first. A derived handler has no such document — its query model belongs to the application and may not even live in this database — so without this record its progress is unobservable and a caller cannot wait for it at all. Written after the handler's own write succeeds, never before. A crash between the two leaves the checkpoint behind, which reports "not yet" and is repaired by the next at-least-once redelivery; the reverse order would report a query model as caught up that never received the event. Remarks Monotonic: a redelivered older position leaves the checkpoint where it is, so duplicate delivery is a no-op for progress exactly as it is for the query model. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.title: Interface IProjectionWriterContractInspector | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.summary: Interface IProjectionWriterContractInspector Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Persistence Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Reads the evidence a writer-protocol cutover is checked against, without taking part in the protocol. public interface IProjectionWriterContractInspector Remarks This is an operator surface, deliberately separate from IProjectionControlPlaneStore: it never admits the caller, creates or renews a lease, increments the admission counter or promotes the marker. A pre-flight run from a newer binary therefore cannot trigger the cutover it is checking. Liveness is evaluated by MongoDB server time. The three parts are separate reads, not one snapshot; repeat the inspection after a change rather than treating one result as a continuous guarantee. Pre-12 binaries write no writer lease, so for that cutover only capability advertisements are database evidence, and only for hosts that publish capabilities. An empty result never proves that no old process is running. The result identifies deployments, instances and writer leases. Authorize callers as operators; unlike ProjectionWriterContractException, this is not an error message and is not kept anonymous. Methods InspectAsync(CancellationToken) Reads the protocol marker, the live writer leases and the live capability advertisements. Task<ProjectionWriterContractInspection> InspectAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<ProjectionWriterContractInspection> The current evidence; empty collections when nothing is live.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.title: Interface IRawProjectionStallReader | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.summary: Interface IRawProjectionStallReader Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Persistence Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Reads how far the raw layer is behind because an event of a stream never arrived. public interface IRawProjectionStallReader Remarks A separate port rather than another member on IRawProjectionStore: the ingestion port is implemented by consumers who replace the store, and widening it would break every one of them for a purely diagnostic capability. A missing event does not corrupt a read model — the contiguity gate stores later events without applying them, so the aggregate stalls instead of diverging. That is the better failure mode, but only if someone notices; otherwise "stalls instead of diverging" degrades into "diverges silently, one aggregate at a time". Methods GetStallSnapshotAsync(string, int, CancellationToken) Summarizes the events that are stored but not applied because an earlier event of their stream is missing. Returns Task<RawProjectionStallSnapshot> The current stall snapshot for this aggregate. Remarks Storing and applying happen in one transaction, so an event that is externally visible as unapplied is genuinely waiting for a predecessor rather than merely in flight.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.summary: Class MongoProjectionStore Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Persistence Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Implements transactional, aggregate-specific MongoDB projection persistence. public sealed class MongoProjectionStore : IRawProjectionStore, IProjectionReferenceSource, IMergedProjectionStore, IProjectionStoreMaintenance, IRawProjectionStallReader, IProjectionCheckpointStore, IProjectionControlPlaneStore, IProjectionInvalidationStore, IDerivedProjectionDependencyStore Inheritance object MongoProjectionStore Implements IRawProjectionStore IProjectionReferenceSource IMergedProjectionStore IProjectionStoreMaintenance IRawProjectionStallReader IProjectionCheckpointStore IProjectionControlPlaneStore IProjectionInvalidationStore IDerivedProjectionDependencyStore Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The store is split internally into components that each own one collection or one cohesive state and lifecycle, over one Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Persistence.MongoProjectionStoreContext that carries the database, the writer gate and the options and runs the transactions spanning their collections: the raw layer (RawEvents_* and Raw_*), the merged layer, checkpoints, the invalidation claim ledger, rebuild scans, the control plane (definitions and capabilities), tracked reads, failure evidence, derived attempts, repairs, refolds, the refold request inbox and the retention of finished requests. This class keeps the public surface, owns initialization and writer admission, and delegates everything else. A transaction spanning components is still one MongoDB transaction: folding raw events stays inside the raw layer, and publishing declared reads, joining a repair to the claim ledger, confirming a checkpoint with its repair work and terminating a repair claim are run by Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Persistence.MongoProjectionRepairs, which passes its session to every fenced write of the transaction. The BSON field names and status values every component writes are declared here, once: ProjectionStorageContractTests compares those shared with Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client against these constants by name. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.summary: Class ProjectionEventUnprotector Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Privacy Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Unprotects the tagged values of a stored raw event before it is folded into raw state. This is the one place where ciphertext becomes plaintext on the read side: RawEvents_* keeps what the envelope carried, raw state and merged documents hold what the fold produced. public sealed class ProjectionEventUnprotector Inheritance object ProjectionEventUnprotector Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A destroyed or unknown key is an expected state, not a fault: the tag's own policy supplies the placeholder or removes the property, and the fold continues. An unreachable registry throws SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException out of the fold, which leaves the delivery unsettled for redelivery; a value that does not authenticate throws FieldProtectionException, which the raw processor dead-letters because no retry can repair an altered ciphertext. Without a registered ISubjectKeyRegistry the unprotector is inert until the first tagged value arrives; that value is then refused with a configuration error rather than folded as ciphertext, because a read model that holds tags instead of plaintext is a read model no query can use. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.title: Interface IProjectionHandler | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.summary: Interface IProjectionHandler Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Projections Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Builds one application-owned query model on top of the framework-standard raw and merged layers. public interface IProjectionHandler Remarks The raw and merged layers are configuration-only and identical for every application. A derived handler is where code belongs: traversals, aggregations, denormalizations and anything a configured reference join cannot express. Handlers run in their own consumer stage, so a failing handler dead-letters its own message and never blocks the merged layer. A handler that throws is retried by the transport; a handler that keeps throwing ends in the aggregate's dead-letter destination. Properties DefinitionVersion Gets the application-controlled version of this projection definition. string DefinitionVersion { get; } Property Value string Remarks Keep this opaque token stable for unchanged semantics, and increment it when a transformation or output-shape change may require existing query model documents to be recomputed. It is part of the shared registry snapshot and deliberately remains independent of the handler class, assembly version, deployment revision, and storage location. This version fences invalidations, failure attempts, checkpoints, dependencies, and barriers. Publishing a changed version schedules a resumable scan over current merged inputs, while the fence ensures its work and progress cannot inherit old-definition evidence. The scan schedules recomputation, not output-schema migration: insert-if-absent leaves existing documents unchanged even after successful handler completion. Use an idempotent replacement or selective upsert that actually migrates existing output, preserving application-owned immutable values. Scans cover current surviving inputs, not deleted inputs or historical per-event moments. Scan completion means work was durably scheduled; it does not certify handler completion or inspect application collections. ProjectionName Gets the stable public name of the query model this handler maintains. string ProjectionName { get; } Property Value string Remarks This is what a caller asks progress by, and what it stores in a frozen consistency selection. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.W.summary: Class ProjectionStallDetector Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Workers Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Samples the stored-but-unapplied events of every configured aggregate and reports them as metrics and, past a configured age, as a warning. public sealed class ProjectionStallDetector : BackgroundService, IHostedService, IDisposable Inheritance object BackgroundService ProjectionStallDetector Implements IHostedService IDisposable Inherited Members BackgroundService.StartAsync(CancellationToken) BackgroundService.StopAsync(CancellationToken) BackgroundService.Dispose() BackgroundService.ExecuteTask object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The pipeline applies raw events only in contiguous sequence, so a missing event leaves later ones stored and unapplied: the aggregate stalls rather than diverging. That is the better failure mode and it is the reason a global read cursor was judged unnecessary — but it only holds while someone notices the stall. Nothing else in the pipeline does: the raw processor settles the message and adds zero to the applied counter, and the pending-notification sweep only looks at events that were already applied. Detection is separate from repair on purpose. Repair is an operator-triggered replay through the outbox, which reaches every consumer of the affected streams; this worker never triggers one, it only makes the need visible. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.summary: Class AggregateRoutingCatalogExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.Catalog Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.dll Contributes configured routes to the event contract catalogue. public static class AggregateRoutingCatalogExtensions Inheritance object AggregateRoutingCatalogExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Contract names come from code; stream names do not. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.summary: Class EventSourcingDddServiceCollectionExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.DependencyInjection Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.dll Registers Direct mode end to end: the PostgreSQL event store, aggregate routing, and every DDD persistence port implemented over them. public static class EventSourcingDddServiceCollectionExtensions Inheritance object EventSourcingDddServiceCollectionExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods AddDevboneEventSourcing(IServiceCollection, EventStoreSettings, AggregateRoutingOptions, EventPublicationContext) Registers the event store and the DDD persistence ports for Direct mode. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneEventSourcing(this IServiceCollection services, EventStoreSettings settings, AggregateRoutingOptions routing, EventPublicationContext publicationContext) Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. settings EventStoreSettings Validated event-store settings. routing AggregateRoutingOptions Aggregate routing resolved and snapshotted onto every commit. publicationContext EventPublicationContext Producer and trace context stamped onto every outbox envelope. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks Everything registered here is a singleton. The adapter is stateless; the event store owns a connection factory and no per-request state. It registers an EventStoreIdentity with the EventStoreId the routes name; an outbox dispatcher registered beside it must name the same store. This does not register a bus or an outbox dispatcher. Persistence and publication are separate concerns: a commit is durable once the event and its outbox row are written, and delivery is a later, independently retried step. It does register the canonical envelope serializer, because an outbox row carries an envelope and the mapper cannot be constructed without one. The registration uses TryAdd, so an application that registers its own serializer keeps it, and calling AddDevboneEventBus as well does not produce a second instance - the bytes written to an outbox row and the bytes published must be identical. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when an argument is null. InvalidOperationException Thrown when the routing is invalid, or when its route versions name more than one event store: Direct mode writes every aggregate to the one store registered here.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.summary: Class EventPrivacyCatalogCheck Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.Privacy Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.dll Verifies at startup, against the generated contract catalogue, that every protected privacy field is a string and that a field removed on erasure is nullable and optional. The store enforces the same at commit; this check fails composition instead of the first command. public static class EventPrivacyCatalogCheck Inheritance object EventPrivacyCatalogCheck Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods FindGaps(IReadOnlyCollection<EventPrivacyDefinition>, IReadOnlyCollection<string>?, IReadOnlyList<EventContractDescriptor>?) Compares the registered definitions with the catalogue in both directions and lists every gap: a catalogue contract without a definition, a definition without a catalogue contract, a definition field path that is not a field of its contract, and a catalogue field neither classified by a definition nor declared non-personal. Under field protection a missing definition is an unprotected field, which is why an application keeps this as a build-time test beside its definitions. public static EventPrivacyCatalogGaps FindGaps(IReadOnlyCollection<EventPrivacyDefinition> definitions, IReadOnlyCollection<string>? nonPersonalFields = null, IReadOnlyList<EventContractDescriptor>? catalogue = null) Parameters definitions IReadOnlyCollection<EventPrivacyDefinition> The registered definitions. A definition with classification None declares its whole contract non-personal. nonPersonalFields IReadOnlyCollection<string> Fields the application has assessed as non-personal, as <contract>:<path>, for example order.created:total; a path covers everything below it. catalogue IReadOnlyList<EventContractDescriptor> The catalogue; defaults to the generated one. Returns EventPrivacyCatalogGaps The gaps; IsComplete when there are none. Remarks A contract is matched by name and, when the catalogue records a version, by version; a definition path classifies every field below it. An array of objects is enumerated per element member with the element wildcard (Loans[].BorrowerName), and a path to the array itself (Loans) covers all of them; scalar arrays, maps and objects beyond the catalogue's nesting depth count as one field. Verify(IReadOnlyCollection<EventPrivacyDefinition>, IReadOnlyList<EventContractDescriptor>?) Verifies the protected fields of every definition against the catalogue. public static void Verify(IReadOnlyCollection<EventPrivacyDefinition> definitions, IReadOnlyList<EventContractDescriptor>? catalogue = null) Parameters definitions IReadOnlyCollection<EventPrivacyDefinition> The registered definitions. catalogue IReadOnlyList<EventContractDescriptor> The catalogue; defaults to the generated one. Remarks The catalogue describes the current write version of each contract only. A definition for that version is verified; a definition for an earlier version is kept for events already stored, governs no write and is skipped, because the current shape says nothing about the old one. A catalogue without versions verifies every definition, as before. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when a contract with protected fields is not in the catalogue, a definition names a version newer than the catalogue's, a protected path is not in the contract (including a path into an array without the element wildcard), is not a string, or is removed on erasure while it is required or not nullable.

Disabled when null or empty, which is the default. public string? StreamNamingConvention { get; init; } Property Value string Remarks On a broker shared by several applications, stream names are a cross-application namespace that nothing otherwise reserves or validates. Two applications can silently choose the same stream; each then publishes into the other's topic and consumes events it cannot interpret. A convention such as ^myapp\.[a-z0-9-]+\.events$ makes that collision impossible to configure by accident. The framework enforces the pattern, not the pattern's content: choosing and reserving the namespace is a platform-operations responsibility. Default off so an existing deployment is unaffected until it opts in. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Loc.title: Interface IAggregateLockLease | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Loc.summary: Interface IAggregateLockLease Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Locks Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.dll Represents exclusive ownership of one aggregate advisory lock. Disposing the lease asynchronously releases the owning PostgreSQL session lock exactly once. public interface IAggregateLockLease : IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync() Remarks The lease is released with await using or DisposeAsync(). A synchronous Dispose was removed in Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing 22.0.0: the release runs pg_advisory_unlock on the lease's session, and a synchronous release blocked a thread on that round trip. Properties Info Gets immutable metadata describing this lock ownership. AggregateLockInfo Info { get; } Property Value AggregateLockInfo IsReleased Gets a value indicating whether ownership has already been released explicitly, by disposing this lease. bool IsReleased { get; } Property Value bool Remarks It reports the holder's own release only. A lease whose PostgreSQL session ended underneath it still reports false here; IsHeldAsync(CancellationToken) is the member that can see that. Methods IsHeldAsync(CancellationToken) Checks whether this lease still holds its lock, including whether the session holding it is still alive. ValueTask<bool> IsHeldAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token for the check. Returns ValueTask<bool> true when the lock is still held; false after an explicit release or when the session that held it is gone. Remarks Added in Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing 20.3.0. A session advisory lock lives exactly as long as its session: a server restart, a failover, pg_terminate_backend, idle_session_timeout or a dropped connection releases it without the holder noticing. The leases of EventStore answer with one trivial round trip on the lease's own session, so a live session means a held lock; any failure means the lock is gone, and that answer is final. The default implementation can only see an explicit release and returns IsReleased == false. Exceptions OperationCanceledException cancellationToken was cancelled.

Do not confuse it with Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Repositories.IAggregateLockPort, the application-facing DDD port that is strongly typed over aggregate identity and owns the bounded retry policy. An adapter implements that port over this store; application and domain code uses the port, not this type. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Out.summary: Interface IOutboxRequeue Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Outbox Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.dll Returns a terminally failed outbox row to dispatch. A failed row blocks every later event of its aggregate, because the claim delivers an aggregate's events in order; once the cause is fixed - a broker that was unreachable for longer than a configured attempt limit, a missing topic or exchange - an operator requeues it and the aggregate resumes. The stored envelope is published unchanged; a row whose envelope cannot be read or does not match its columns fails again on its first attempt. public interface IOutboxRequeue Methods RequeueFailedAsync(string, CancellationToken) Moves one Failed row back to Pending, due immediately and with its attempt count reset; the last error is kept for diagnosis until the next attempt replaces it. Task<bool> RequeueFailedAsync(string eventId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters eventId string The event identifier of the outbox row. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<bool> true when the row was failed and is pending again; false when no row with that identifier exists or it is not failed, in which case nothing changed.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Out.summary: Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Outbox Classes ClaimedOutboxMessage Represents an outbox message leased to one dispatcher attempt. OutboxClaimRequest Defines one bounded request for leasing dispatchable outbox messages. OutboxMessage Represents an immutable, route-stable event envelope to persist with an event-store commit. OutboxPublication Describes a transport-confirmed outbox publication. OutboxRetry Describes a retry scheduled after an outbox publication failure. Interfaces IOutboxNotificationListener Waits for database-level hints that dispatchable outbox work may be available. IOutboxRequeue Returns a terminally failed outbox row to dispatch. A failed row blocks every later event of its aggregate, because the claim delivers an aggregate's events in order; once the cause is fixed - a broker that was unreachable for longer than a configured attempt limit, a missing topic or exchange - an operator requeues it and the aggregate resumes. The stored envelope is published unchanged; a row whose envelope cannot be read or does not match its columns fails again on its first attempt. IOutboxStateReader Reads a consistent durable outbox inventory independently of dispatch operations. IOutboxStore Defines durable lease and settlement operations for transactional outbox dispatch. ITransactionalOutboxEventStore Extends event persistence with an outbox write in the same database transaction.
