api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Pri.summary: Class EventPayloadFieldProtector Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Privacy Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.dll Protects the fields a registered definition marks as protected in a serialized event payload, and unprotects the tagged values of stored payloads. Both adapters, Direct mode and the Gateway, run their payloads through this class so that protection happens once, at one place, before the envelope and the database row exist. public sealed class EventPayloadFieldProtector Inheritance object EventPayloadFieldProtector Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The protector resolves keys through the registry it is given and never caches them itself; the caching registry of Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy is what a host registers. A registry that cannot be reached throws SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException out of every method, which a write side surfaces as a rejected commit. A destroyed or unknown key is not a failure: unprotection yields the placeholder the tag carries. Constructors EventPayloadFieldProtector(EventStoreSettings, ISubjectKeyRegistry) Creates the protector over the definitions of one event store. public EventPayloadFieldProtector(EventStoreSettings settings, ISubjectKeyRegistry registry) Parameters settings EventStoreSettings Validated settings; their PrivacyDefinitions decide which fields are protected. registry ISubjectKeyRegistry The subject key registry. Fields WITHHELD_PLACEHOLDER The value UnprotectForSubjectsAsync(IReadOnlyList<PrivacyEventRecord>, IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyReference>, CancellationToken) puts in place of a protected field that belongs to a subject the record is not disclosed to. public const string WITHHELD_PLACEHOLDER = "[withheld]" Field Value string Methods ProtectAsync(IReadOnlyList<EventPayloadProtectionRequest>, int, CancellationToken) Protects the payloads of one commit. public Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> ProtectAsync(IReadOnlyList<EventPayloadProtectionRequest> events, int maximumPayloadBytes, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters events IReadOnlyList<EventPayloadProtectionRequest> The events, in commit order. maximumPayloadBytes int The payload size limit the write side enforces; re-checked here because a tagged value is longer than its plaintext. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> One payload per event, in input order; a payload without protected fields is returned as given. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when a protected field is not a string, names a subject the descriptor does not carry or carries more than once, when any string parses as a tag already, when a personal event has no tenant, or when a protected payload exceeds the size limit. SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException Thrown when the registry cannot be reached. UnprotectAsync(IReadOnlyList<IDatabaseEvent>, CancellationToken) Unprotects the payloads of stored events, returning copies with the payload replaced. public Task<IReadOnlyList<IDatabaseEvent>> UnprotectAsync(IReadOnlyList<IDatabaseEvent> events, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters events IReadOnlyList<IDatabaseEvent> The stored events. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<IReadOnlyList<IDatabaseEvent>> Copies in input order; an event without tags is returned as the same instance. UnprotectAsync(IReadOnlyList<string>, CancellationToken) Unprotects every tagged value of the given payloads. Tags are self-describing, so no definition is needed. public Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> UnprotectAsync(IReadOnlyList<string> payloads, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters payloads IReadOnlyList<string> The stored payloads. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> One payload per input, in input order; a payload without tags is returned as given. Exceptions SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException Thrown when the registry cannot be reached. FieldProtectionException Thrown when a tagged value does not authenticate or has an unsupported format. UnprotectForSubjectsAsync(IReadOnlyList<PrivacyEventRecord>, IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyReference>, CancellationToken) Unprotects stored personal-data records for disclosure to some subjects, for example a data-subject access request: a protected field is decrypted only when the record's definition and descriptor assign it to one of subjects; every other tagged value is replaced by WITHHELD_PLACEHOLDER. public Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> UnprotectForSubjectsAsync(IReadOnlyList<PrivacyEventRecord> records, IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyReference> subjects, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters records IReadOnlyList<PrivacyEventRecord> The stored records, as the privacy index loaded them. subjects IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyReference> The subjects the records are disclosed to. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> One payload per record, in input order. Remarks A record found for one subject can carry protected fields of another, such as both parties of a loan. UnprotectAsync(IReadOnlyList<string>, CancellationToken) decrypts every tag whose key is alive and would hand the other party's data to the requester. The assignment follows the rule protection used: field path, subject type and role from the definition, the one matching subject from the descriptor, in the record's tenant. A tag the definition does not assign to a requested subject, including one under an unknown definition, is withheld. A destroyed key of a requested subject yields its tag's placeholder, as anywhere. Fields that were never protected are returned as stored; this method decides only about ciphertext. Exceptions SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException Thrown when the registry cannot be reached. FieldProtectionException Thrown when a requested subject's tagged value does not authenticate.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Res.summary: Class ResendRequest Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Resend Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.dll Describes one operator-requested replay of already published outbox envelopes. public sealed class ResendRequest Inheritance object ResendRequest Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A resend republishes the exact bytes persisted in the outbox, never a reconstructed envelope. That is what makes it safe: a projection recognizes a byte-identical event by its identifier and skips it, so replaying events a read model already has is a no-op rather than a corruption. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Sql.summary: Class EventStoreSchema Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Sql Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.dll Provides the canonical PostgreSQL schema script shipped inside this package and the schema version the assembly expects to find in a database it writes to. public static class EventStoreSchema Inheritance object EventStoreSchema Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The script is also packed as a plain file at sql/postgres/schema.sql inside the NuGet package for database processes that never execute .NET code. Both copies are the same file. Fields DEFAULT_SCHEMA_TABLE_NAME Gets the default name of the single-row table holding the applied schema version. public const string DEFAULT_SCHEMA_TABLE_NAME = "event_store_schema" Field Value string SCHEMA_VERSION Gets the schema version this assembly requires. A database created by GetPostgresScript() reports this value from its schema table. public const int SCHEMA_VERSION = 8 Field Value int Methods GetPostgresMigration3To4Script() Reads the PostgreSQL script that upgrades a schema version 3 database to version 4, the field protection model of privacy definitions. public static string GetPostgresMigration3To4Script() Returns string The upgrade script. Run it exactly once, with every writer stopped, against a database that reports version 3; it verifies the version and refuses definitions it cannot map, naming them. The same file is packed as sql/postgres/migrate-3-to-4.sql. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when the assembly was built without the embedded resource. GetPostgresMigration4To5Script() Reads the PostgreSQL script that upgrades a schema version 4 database to version 5, which makes the database enforce that the first aggregate revision starts at event sequence 1 and only it does. public static string GetPostgresMigration4To5Script() Returns string The upgrade script. Run it exactly once against a database that reports version 4; writers may keep running. It verifies the version, refuses streams that already violate the rule, naming them, and changes no row. The same file is packed as sql/postgres/migrate-4-to-5.sql. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when the assembly was built without the embedded resource. GetPostgresMigration5To6Script() Reads the PostgreSQL script that upgrades a schema version 5 database to version 6, which adds the index that lets a stream be loaded by its aggregate identity alone without scanning the events table. public static string GetPostgresMigration5To6Script() Returns string The upgrade script. Run it exactly once against a database that reports version 5. It verifies the version, builds the index inside its transaction - blocking writes to the events table meanwhile - and changes no row. For a large table, create the index first with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS as the script header shows; the script then only moves the version. The same file is packed as sql/postgres/migrate-5-to-6.sql. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when the assembly was built without the embedded resource. GetPostgresMigration7To8Script() Reads the PostgreSQL script that upgrades a schema version 7 database to version 8, which indexes the outbox for the claim, the replay read and the inventory, so none of them reads the whole, ever-growing table. public static string GetPostgresMigration7To8Script() Returns string The upgrade script. Run it exactly once against a database that reports version 7. It verifies the version, builds the indexes inside its transaction - blocking writes to the outbox, and with them every commit, meanwhile - replaces IX_event_outbox_dispatch and changes no row. For a large table, create the indexes first with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS as the script header shows. The same file is packed as sql/postgres/migrate-7-to-8.sql. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when the assembly was built without the embedded resource. GetPostgresScript() Reads the complete PostgreSQL schema script for a new database. public static string GetPostgresScript() Returns string The DDL script creating the current schema. Run it exactly once against an empty database; it is deliberately not an upgrade migration and must not be applied to a database that already contains event-store tables. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when the assembly was built without the embedded schema resource. MigrateUniqueValueHashes6To7Async(NpgsqlConnection, string, CancellationToken) Upgrades a schema version 6 database to version 7 by keying every stored unique-value hash. Unlike the earlier upgrades this one cannot be a SQL script: it needs the key, which is held outside the database. public static Task<int> MigrateUniqueValueHashes6To7Async(NpgsqlConnection connection, string uniqueValueHashKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters connection NpgsqlConnection An open connection to the event-store database, using the default table names. uniqueValueHashKey string The UniqueValueHashKey every writer of this event store is configured with. cancellationToken CancellationToken The cancellation token. Returns Task<int> The number of rewritten hashes. Remarks Run it exactly once, with every writer stopped, against a database that reports version 6. In one transaction it rewrites each unkeyed SHA-512 digest to h1: plus HMAC-SHA512(key, digest), adds CK_uniques_value_hash_keyed so no writer can store an unkeyed hash afterwards, and moves the version to 7; no other row changes. The digest is not kept, so the key cannot be rotated later without the plaintext values. sql/postgres/migrate-6-to-7.sql documents the same steps for review. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when connection is null. ArgumentException Thrown when the key is missing, not base64, or shorter than 32 bytes. InvalidOperationException Thrown when the database does not report schema version 6. ReadAppliedVersionAsync(NpgsqlConnection, string, string?, CancellationToken) Reads the schema version currently applied to one database. public static Task<int?> ReadAppliedVersionAsync(NpgsqlConnection connection, string schemaTableName = "event_store_schema", string? databaseSchema = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters connection NpgsqlConnection An open connection to the event-store database. schemaTableName string The schema table name. Defaults to DEFAULT_SCHEMA_TABLE_NAME. databaseSchema string The optional PostgreSQL schema qualifying the table. cancellationToken CancellationToken The cancellation token. Returns Task<int?> The applied schema version, or null when the schema table does not exist, which is the case for a database created before the schema table was introduced. Remarks Compare the result with SCHEMA_VERSION before the first write. This is an explicit operation on a caller-owned connection: the event store never opens a connection on construction.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Tim.summary: Class DatabaseOperationGuard Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.TimeMachine.Data Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.TimeMachine.dll Coalesces the initial database probe and suppresses repeated operations while PostgreSQL is unreachable, until it is explicitly retried. public sealed class DatabaseOperationGuard Inheritance object DatabaseOperationGuard Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Only a failure to reach the database opens the circuit. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Tim.summary: Class ResendRequestWriter Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.TimeMachine.Data Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.TimeMachine.dll Records an operator-requested outbox replay. The Time Machine never publishes. public sealed class ResendRequestWriter Inheritance object ResendRequestWriter Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks This is the single write the diagnostics UI is allowed to perform, and it is deliberately narrow: one insert into the resend-request table, nothing else. The Time Machine has no broker credentials and no access to event, outbox, snapshot or privacy writes. Execution happens in the application instances that host the resend worker, which claim the request and publish under their own identity. Keeping request and execution apart is what makes this safe to embed: a UI that could publish would give every application hosting diagnostics the ability to flood a shared broker. [Range(1, 500)] public int DefaultPageSize { get; set; } Property Value int EnableResendRequests Gets or sets whether operators may request an outbox replay from the diagnostics UI. Disabled by default. public bool EnableResendRequests { get; set; } Property Value bool Remarks Even when enabled the Time Machine only records a request; it never publishes. Execution belongs to the application instances hosting the resend worker, which are the only processes with broker credentials. That separation is why a diagnostics UI embedded in an application can offer this at all. A replay reaches every consumer of the affected streams, including other applications on a shared broker. Enabling this therefore requires ResendAuthorizationPolicy; configuration validation rejects the combination of an enabled feature and an unset policy at startup. api/Devbone.Frameworks.Hosting.Health.De.summary: Class DevboneHealthEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Hosting.Health Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Hosting.dll Maps the anonymous liveness and readiness endpoints an orchestrator probes. public static class DevboneHealthEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions Inheritance object DevboneHealthEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Both answer with nothing but the aggregated status, {"status":"Healthy"}, Degraded or Unhealthy: no check names, descriptions, exceptions, durations, hosts or tenants, because the endpoints are anonymous. Why a check failed reaches the host's log through the health check service, never the response. Both endpoints carry IAllowAnonymous metadata, so a host that authenticates every request honours the probes by that standard marker. Methods MapDevboneHealth(IEndpointRouteBuilder, Action<DevboneHealthOptions>?) Maps the liveness endpoint, which runs no check, and the readiness endpoint, which runs every check tagged READINESS_TAG. Healthy and degraded answer 200, unhealthy answers 503. Requires services.AddHealthChecks(); packages contribute their checks to the builder it returns. public static IEndpointRouteBuilder MapDevboneHealth(this IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints, Action<DevboneHealthOptions>? configure = null) Parameters endpoints IEndpointRouteBuilder The route builder. configure Action<DevboneHealthOptions> Adjusts the paths after they were read from the SECTION_NAME section. Returns IEndpointRouteBuilder The same route builder. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when endpoints is null. InvalidOperationException Thrown when a path is invalid or the health check services are not registered.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.Hosting.Telemetry.summary: Class DevboneTelemetryServiceCollectionExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Hosting.Telemetry Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Hosting.dll Registers OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs for the platform's instrumentation and exports them over OTLP, configured by the standard OTEL_* variables. Without OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT nothing is registered and nothing is exported, so the libraries' sources and meters stay as inactive as they are without this package. public static class DevboneTelemetryServiceCollectionExtensions Inheritance object DevboneTelemetryServiceCollectionExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Fields LOGS_EXPORTER_KEY The standard OpenTelemetry variable selecting the log exporter. otlp (or no value) exports logs, none does not; any other value is refused at startup, because this package offers no other exporter. public const string LOGS_EXPORTER_KEY = "OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER" Field Value string NO_EXPORTER The LOGS_EXPORTER_KEY value that exports no logs. public const string NO_EXPORTER = "none" Field Value string OTLP_ENDPOINT_KEY The standard OpenTelemetry variable naming the collector; its presence switches telemetry on. public const string OTLP_ENDPOINT_KEY = "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT" Field Value string OTLP_EXPORTER The LOGS_EXPORTER_KEY value that exports logs over OTLP. public const string OTLP_EXPORTER = "otlp" Field Value string PLATFORM_INSTRUMENTATION_PATTERN The stable prefix every platform activity source and meter starts with. A host subscribing to it observes exactly the platform packages it loads, including ones it loads later, and references none of them. public const string PLATFORM_INSTRUMENTATION_PATTERN = "Devbone.Frameworks.*" Field Value string SERVICE_NAME_KEY The standard OpenTelemetry variable naming the service. public const string SERVICE_NAME_KEY = "OTEL_SERVICE_NAME" Field Value string Methods AddDevboneTelemetry(IServiceCollection, IConfiguration, Action<DevboneTelemetryOptions>?) Registers tracing, metrics and, unless switched off, logging with OTLP export when OTLP_ENDPOINT_KEY is configured. The exporter reads endpoint, protocol, headers and timeout from the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* settings. Subscribes to PLATFORM_INSTRUMENTATION_PATTERN, the configured additional sources and meters, and the ASP.NET Core server instrumentation; request spans keep the route template (http.route) and lose the concrete path and the query string. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneTelemetry(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration, Action<DevboneTelemetryOptions>? configure = null) Parameters services IServiceCollection The host's services. configuration IConfiguration The host's configuration, environment variables included. configure Action<DevboneTelemetryOptions> Adds the host's own sources and meters, a default service name, or switches log export off. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when services or configuration is null. InvalidOperationException Thrown when an option is invalid or LOGS_EXPORTER_KEY names an exporter other than OTLP_EXPORTER or NO_EXPORTER; both are checked with or without an endpoint, so a mistake fails on the first start rather than on the first start with a collector.

A 4xx status with the service's error body is SubjectKeyRegistryException with that body's code. Logs carry status and code, never a subject reference and never material. Constructors SubjectKeyServiceClient(HttpClient, SubjectKeyServiceClientOptions, ILogger<SubjectKeyServiceClient>?) Creates the client. public SubjectKeyServiceClient(HttpClient httpClient, SubjectKeyServiceClientOptions options, ILogger<SubjectKeyServiceClient>? logger = null) Parameters httpClient HttpClient A client whose base address points at the key service. options SubjectKeyServiceClientOptions Validated options. logger ILogger<SubjectKeyServiceClient> Optional logger. Methods DestroyAsync(SubjectKeyReference, string, CancellationToken) Destroys the subject's active key. Idempotent: a repeated call returns the first destruction. public Task<SubjectKeyDestruction> DestroyAsync(SubjectKeyReference subject, string reason, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters subject SubjectKeyReference The subject. reason string The reason recorded in the audit row. The row is kept for good as the lasting record of the destruction, so pass the erasure case reference, an identifier that names no person. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<SubjectKeyDestruction> The destruction record. Exceptions SubjectKeyRegistryException Thrown with SUBJECT_UNKNOWN when the subject never had a key, or when the registry rejects the request. SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException Thrown when the registry cannot be reached. GetOrCreateAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyReference>, CancellationToken) Returns the active key of every subject, creating one for a subject that never had a key. A subject whose key was destroyed gets no new key: the whole batch is refused with SUBJECT_ERASED and no key is created for any subject of it. public Task<IReadOnlyList<SubjectKeyMaterial>> GetOrCreateAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyReference> subjects, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters subjects IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyReference> The subjects, at most MAXIMUM_BATCH_SIZE. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<IReadOnlyList<SubjectKeyMaterial>> One key per subject, in input order. Remarks Before 2.0.0 a destroyed subject silently received a new key, so a write about an erased person stored data that could be read again. A key subject is never reused; an application treats a write about an erased subject as erased, refusing it or writing without that subject's data. The refusal is not retryable. Exceptions SubjectKeyRegistryException Thrown when the registry rejects the request, with SUBJECT_ERASED when a subject's key was destroyed. SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException Thrown when the registry cannot be reached. ResolveAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyId>, CancellationToken) Resolves key identifiers found in tagged values. public Task<IReadOnlyList<SubjectKeyResolution>> ResolveAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyId> keyIds, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters keyIds IReadOnlyCollection<SubjectKeyId> The identifiers, at most MAXIMUM_BATCH_SIZE. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<IReadOnlyList<SubjectKeyResolution>> One resolution per identifier, in input order. Exceptions SubjectKeyRegistryException Thrown when the registry rejects the request. SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException Thrown when the registry cannot be reached.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy.Keys.html.title: Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy.Keys | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy.Keys.html.summary: Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy.Keys Classes CachingSubjectKeyRegistry Caches registry answers per caller, bounded in time by the registry's window and the caller's own maximum, and bounded in size. A destruction through this instance evicts immediately; a destruction elsewhere becomes visible when the cached answer expires, which is the window the guide states. InMemorySubjectKeyRegistry A registry held in process memory, for tests of the write side, the worker and application code. It keeps the semantics of the key service: get-or-create is idempotent and race-safe, a destroyed subject that returns receives a new key, destruction is idempotent, and an unavailable registry throws SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException rather than answering. SubjectKeyBatch Validates registry request batches the same way in every implementation, so that a registry of the application's own (over a KMS, for example) rejects what the platform's registries reject. SubjectKeyCacheOptions Bounds the per-caller key cache of CachingSubjectKeyRegistry. SubjectKeyDestruction The audit record of a key destruction. It carries no key material and no subject reference; the identifier is opaque. SubjectKeyErrorCodes The stable error codes of the key registry and the key service wire contract. SubjectKeyMaterial An active subject key with its material, as returned to a caller that protects values. SubjectKeyReference Identifies the data subject a key belongs to: the pseudonymized triple the event privacy index already records per event. The same triple names the same key, so the reference must be stable and must never be a raw personal value. SubjectKeyRegistryException The registry answered and rejected the request. The message never contains key material or a subject reference. SubjectKeyRegistryUnavailableException The registry could not be reached or could not answer. A write side rejects its commit; a reader leaves its delivery unsettled and retries. Never a dead letter, never a placeholder. SubjectKeyResolution The registry's answer for one key identifier a reader asked about. Structs SubjectKeyId The registry-assigned identifier of one subject key: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. It is never derived from the subject reference, so a tag carrying it reveals nothing about the subject. Interfaces ISubjectKeyRegistry The registry of subject keys. One key per subject reference; destruction is the erasure of everything protected with it. Enums SubjectKeyState The state of a subject key as the registry reports it.

index.html.summary: Devbone Event-Driven Platform — API reference Generated from the XML documentation of the published packages. Every public type is here because missing documentation is a build error in this platform, not a warning. This reference answers what a type is and how it behaves. It does not explain how to stand an application up — that is the narrative guide, which lives with the source. Packages Package Purpose Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd Domain model, aggregates, commands, event contracts, privacy contracts, snapshot-facing ports. Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Testing In-memory persistence ports and a Given/When/Then aggregate harness. Development dependency. Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing PostgreSQL event store, optimistic concurrency, privacy index, snapshots, transactional outbox. Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd Direct-mode adapter over the event store, aggregate routing, stored-event mappers. Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.TimeMachine Read-only diagnostics UI as a Razor class library. Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Contracts Broker-independent canonical envelope, metadata, lifecycle, privacy, headers. Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus Transport-neutral publish/subscribe and manual settlement; carries no broker client. Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Kafka Apache Kafka transport for the event bus. Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.RabbitMq RabbitMQ transport for the event bus. Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox Claim, publish, retry and settle dispatcher over the outbox port. Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence.Contracts Transport-neutral gateway wire contracts. Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence.Client Optional persistence-port adapter over HTTPS. Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence.Gateway The Event Persistence Gateway as a library: authentication, routing, persistence, locks and the embedded outbox dispatchers. Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection Kafka/RabbitMQ-to-MongoDB read pipeline: raw, merged and derived layers. Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.MongoDb Shared JSON/BSON conversion, compatibility and size limits. Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Kafka Apache Kafka transport for the projection pipeline. Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.RabbitMq RabbitMQ transport for the projection pipeline. Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Client Bounded, opt-in read-your-writes waiting for API hosts. Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy Per-subject data keys and field protection: registry, protector, tagged value format, key service client. Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy.KeyService The key service as a library: endpoints, authentication, and the PostgreSQL registry of wrapped keys. Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy.Requests The application side of data-subject requests: the endpoints a platform privacy service calls, the caller policy, two-phase erasure and export. Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy.Requests.EventProjection The refold step of data-subject erasure: places refold requests for the projection worker through EventProjection.Client, so the API host never becomes a projection writer. Devbone.Frameworks.Privacy.Requests.EventSourcing The event-store steps of data-subject requests: finds the aggregates of a subject through the privacy index, deletes their snapshots under the aggregate lock, and exports the records decrypted for the person with the protected fields of other people withheld. Devbone.Frameworks.Hosting Optional hosting conventions: OpenTelemetry export over OTLP for the Devbone.Frameworks.* instrumentation, and anonymous liveness and readiness probes. The deployable hosts — the projection worker, the persistence gateway, the standalone Time Machine host and the key service host — are services rather than libraries and are deliberately absent.
